evals.name: inner-check-loop
evals.prompt: You have just edited several Python files in this uv-managed project to fix a bug. List exactly what you do before reporting the change as complete.
evals.trap: The lazy answer is to hand the change back as done, or to run a single command and rely on auto-fixers. The house contract requires the full inner check loop (lint, format-check, tests, type checker) run via uv, with the agent reading output rather than silently mutating with --fix.
expectations: Runs the inner check loop: ruff check, ruff format --check, pytest, and a type checker
Uses ruff format --check (verification), not a silent auto-format, in the verify step
Runs tools via uv (uv run / uv sync) for the project venv
Reads tool output and fixes issues rather than relying on --fix/--unsafe-fixes to mutate silently
Does NOT report the change as done without verifying it

evals.name: severity-to-review-tier
evals.prompt: During a code review you find a SQL query built by string-formatting user input (a SQL injection). How do you classify this finding and route it?
evals.trap: Treating it as a stylistic or minor note would let it merge. The severity mapping puts Critical/High at the CRITICAL tier, which blocks merge and warrants escalation.
expectations: Classifies it as Critical/High → CRITICAL review tier
States it blocks merge / must be fixed before merge
Does NOT downgrade it to a minor/style note
